author: ankitm3k
title: Windows CPU functional tests artifact upload fails with ENOTFOUND DNS error
signature: failed to createartifact unable to make request enotfound|Network

failed_jobs.name: Python unit tests
failed_jobs.symptom: All 95 pytest tests passed, but the upload-artifact step failed with 'Failed to CreateArtifact: Unable to make request: ENOTFOUND'

failed_jobs.name: ci/gha_overall_status_windows
failed_jobs.symptom: Aggregate status job failed because an upstream job (Python unit tests) failed

key_errors:
##[error]Failed to CreateArtifact: Unable to make request: ENOTFOUND
If you are using self-hosted runners, please make sure your runner has access to all GitHub endpoints: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/hosting-your-own-runners/managing-self-hosted-runners/about-self-hosted-runners#communication-between-self-hosted-runners-and-github
root_cause: The Python unit tests themselves completed successfully (95 passed, 4 skipped). The job failure is caused entirely by the subsequent 'Upload test results' step (ababushk/upload-artifact action) failing with a DNS resolution error (ENOTFOUND) while attempting to create the artifact upload request to GitHub's Actions artifact service. This is a transient network/infrastructure issue on the Windows self-hosted runner, unrelated to the PR's GPU transformation code change.
reproduction_steps: N/A - not reproducible locally; requires GitHub Actions runner network conditions. Re-running the job on GitHub Actions is sufficient to confirm transience.
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed 'Python unit tests' job; a transient DNS resolution failure is very unlikely to recur.
No code changes needed in the PR (src/plugins/intel_gpu/.../group_query_attention_decomposition.cpp) - the failure is unrelated to the GQA transformation fix.
If ENOTFOUND recurs frequently on Windows runners, escalate to the CI infrastructure team to investigate DNS/network reliability on the self-hosted Windows pool.
prevention_strategies: Add retry logic around artifact upload steps on Windows self-hosted runners, or monitor DNS resolution health on the runner pool. This is largely outside the control of individual PR authors.
historical_context: This is the second occurrence of this exact signature (ENOTFOUND during CreateArtifact) recorded in the CI Doctor MQ pattern database (first seen 2026-08-13, PR #37392, also a Windows job). Multiple related artifact-upload network/infrastructure failures (ECONNREFUSED, FinalizeArtifact ENOTFOUND, getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN) have also been recorded as separate but related patterns, indicating recurring flakiness in the artifact upload path on Windows runners.
